newsitem.title: GERMANY: German soldiers work to bolster dike as hopes rise.
newsitem.headline: German soldiers work to bolster dike as hopes rise.

text.p: About 900 soldiers struggled early on Wednesday to prop up a critical section of a dike on Germany's eastern border as hopes rose that a massive effort in recent days will prevent it bursting and flooding a fertile area.

The soldiers working round-the-clock shifts filled sandbags to help bolster a three-km (two-mile) section of the dike as Brandenburg state officials for the first time in several days began to express hope the dikes would hold.
After nearly two weeks of flood tides, water levels appeared to be receding, giving the first signs of hope that the huge effort waged by thousands of soldiers and aid workers could prove successful.

Some of the worst floods this century have hit Poland and the Czech Republic and 100 people have died in the two countries. While no deaths have been reported in Germany, there has been extensive damage to homes, businesses and farms.
Helicopters each carrying up to five tonnes of sand flew to the most critical spots in the dike that has been under intense pressure after nearly two weeks of some of the worst floods in 200 years.

Brandenburg state officials said a new wave of floods reached the village of Ratzdorf, where the Oder and Neisse rivers that make up Germany's eastern border flow together, but that water levels were well below expectations.
"As a result the serious situation continues," said a state official, but the official added there was a slight ray of hope that the spectacular effort would keep the dam from bursting.
Brandenburg officials breathed a sigh of relieve when lower-than-expected flood waters rushed into the area near Ratzdorf.
But the situation remained tense, as there were still numerous spots in the dike where water had seeped through, making clear that the foundation of the dike remained unsteady.
The most vulnerable spot in the dike that protects the Oderbruch basin area was still near Hohenwutzen, officials said.
No new incidents were reported on Tuesday night as soldiers worked furiously to reinforce the dike that prevents the Oder from spilling into the huge Oderbruch basin.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl visited east German towns threatened by floods on Tuesday, saying the spectacular effort by soldiers, aid workers and townsfolk to keep dikes intact exemplified the unity of east and west Germany.
